Harbour Lantern Stories

Chapter Three: The Lamplighter of Vell

Q01 The lamps along the quay went out one by one.

Q02 Oren counted them from the bell tower stairs.

Q03 Nine lamps, then ten, then the dark harbour.

Q04 He lit his own lantern and started down.

Q05 The steps were wet and smelled of old rope.

Q06 A gull watched him from the broken railing.

Q07 Below, a ferry knocked softly at its post.

Q08 Nobody was meant to be aboard at this hour.

Q09 Yet a window in the cabin glowed faint red.

Q10 Oren raised the lantern and called a greeting.

Q11 The glow went out at once, as if it heard him.

Q12 He stood still and listened to the water.

LONG The ferry had not moved from its post in eleven years, not since the winter the river froze solid from the mill to the sea and the town council voted to leave it where it was rather than pay a crew to haul it out, and in all that time Oren had never once seen a light aboard it, because the cabin doors had been nailed shut by the harbour master himself, with long iron nails that had long since rusted into the wood, so that anybody who wanted to get inside would have needed a crowbar and a great deal of patience and a reason far better than curiosity; he knew all of this the way he knew the number of lamps on the quay and the order in which they went dark, and so when the red glow returned a moment later, steadier this time and lower in the window, as though someone inside had set a candle on the floor and crouched beside it, he did not call out again, but walked very slowly along the edge of the quay, lantern held behind his back to hide its light, until he could see the gap between the hull and the stones and the narrow plank that someone had laid across it, fresh and pale and dry, which had certainly not been there at dusk when he made his first round of the evening and checked every mooring line by hand, and again an hour later, when the tower bell rang nine and the fog began to lift.

Q13 Oren set one foot on the plank and waited.

Q14 It held, though it bowed under his weight.

Q15 The deck was slick with a skin of black ice.

Q16 He crossed it in four long, careful strides.

Q17 The cabin door stood open by a hand's width.

Q18 The nails lay in a neat row on the step.

Q19 Someone had pulled them out without a tool.

Q20 He pushed the door and the hinges sighed.

Q21 Inside, the air was warmer than the night.

Q22 A candle burned in a dish on the floorboards.

Q23 Beside it sat a girl with a chart on her knees.

Q24 She did not look up when the lantern came in.

Q25 "You count the lamps too," she said quietly.

Q26 Oren lowered the lantern and found a stool.

Q27 "Somebody has to," he said. "Who are you?"

Q28 "The one who puts them out," she answered.

Q29 She turned the chart so he could read it.

Q30 Every lamp in Vell was marked in red ink.

Q31 Beside each one was a time, to the minute.

Q32 Tonight's times were already crossed off.

Q33 Tomorrow's column was empty but for one lamp.

Q34 It was the lamp above his own front door.

Q35 "Why that one?" he asked, and she shrugged.

Q36 "It is the last one left that nobody watches."

Q37 Oren thought of his wife asleep beneath it.

Q38 He took the pencil from behind the girl's ear.

Q39 He wrote his own name beside the empty lamp.

Q40 The candle flickered, and the girl smiled.
